AddTrackModel.text:
# AddTrackModel (Widget model, data-management plugin)

## Actions
- `setMixinData(arg: Record<string, unknown>) => void`
- `updateBulkInput(patch: Partial<BulkInputState>) => void`: Patch the bulk workflow's collected input. A patch rather than a setter per field: the bulk form edits several of these together (removing a row rewrites the input *and* forgets that row's rename).
- `setAdapterHint(obj: string) => void`
- `setTextIndexingConf(conf: IndexingAttr) => void`
- `setTextIndexTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setTrackData(obj: FileLocation) => void`
- `setIndexTrackData(obj: FileLocation) => void`
- `setDetectedIndex(obj: FileLocation, name: string) => void`: Records an index found beside the main file. Ignored when an index is already set, since a probe resolving late must never overwrite one typed while it was in flight.
- `setAssembly(str: string) => void`
- `setTrackName(str: string) => void`
- `setTrackType(str: string) => void`
- `clearData() => void`

## Getters
- `trackContainer: TrackContainer | undefined`: The track list a submitted track opens in.
- `trackAdapter: AdapterConfig | undefined`
- `trackName: string`
- `submittableTrackName: string`: The trimmed name the track is added under. Check this one for an all-whitespace entry: `!!trackName` accepts `' '` and creates a track whose name is blank in the selector.
- `uris: (string | undefined)[]`
- `isFtp: boolean`
- `isRelativeUrl: boolean`
- `wrongProtocol: boolean`
- `adapterHintNotConfigurable: boolean`: Returns true if the user selected an adapter from the dropdown but the extension point couldn't build a config for it
- `assembly: string | undefined`
- `trackAdapterType: string | undefined`
- `trackType: string`
- `warningMessage: "" | "Warning: JBrowse cannot access files using the ftp protocol" | …`

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.literal('AddTrackWidget')`
- `view = types.safeReference( pluginManager.pluggableMstType('view', 'stateModel'), )`
- `trackContainerId = types.maybe(types.string)`: Which of the view's track containers the new track opens in, by id. Absent, the usual case, means the view itself. The same property on HierarchicalTrackSelectorWidget sets this one.

## Methods
- `getTrackConfig(timestamp: number) => DraftTrackConfig | undefined`

AppCoreJBrowseModel.text:
# AppCoreJBrowseModel (Root model, core)

built on the [JBrowseRootConfig](/docs/config/jbrowserootconfig) config model — config models are MST trees themselves, which is why this state model is allowed to build on one. Generally found on a property named rootModel.jbrowse

## Actions
- `addAssemblyConf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => ConfigNodeProps<any> & ConfigNodeActions & ConfigNodeBrand<AnyConfigurationSchemaType>`
- `removeAssemblyConf(assemblyName: string) => void`
- `addTrackConf(loose: { trackId: string; type?: string | undefined; }) => { [key: string]: unknown; trackId: string; } | undefined`
- `addConnectionConf(connectionConf: AnyConfiguration) => PluggableConfigNode & IStateTreeNode<PluggableConfigSchemaType>`: Adds to the config's own `connections`, which every visitor to this instance loads. Takes a snapshot as readily as a built config model — the array coerces — since callers hand it plain JSON (a session spec's `sessionConnections`, the…
- `deleteConnectionConf(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => boolean`
- `deleteTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfigurationModel | { trackId: string; }) => void`
- `updateTrackConf(trackConf: { [key: string]: unknown; trackId: string; }) => void`: Updates an existing track configuration. Used to sync editable configs back to the frozen tracks array. A trackId the array repeats replaces its last entry, the one the session resolves it to.
- `addPlugin(pluginDefinition: PluginDefinition) => void`
- `removePlugin(pluginDefinition: PluginDefinition) => void`: Removes the entry that loads from the same url — the version-pinned definition, not every entry sharing a name, so the update flow's remove-then-add swaps one version for another.
- `setDefaultSessionConf(sessionConf: AnyConfigurationModel) => void`: takes the live session or a plain session snapshot
- `addInternetAccountConf(internetAccountConf: AnyConfigurationModel) => PluggableConfigNode & IStateTreeNode<PluggableConfigSchemaType>`
- `deleteInternetAccountConf(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => boolean`

## Getters
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`

# AppSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Session getters shared by the "app" products (desktop + web) that simply delegate to the root model — `version`, `history`, `menus`, `assemblyManager` — plus `renameCurrentSession`. Centralized here so the products compose one mixin instead of re-declaring (and diverging on) the same root delegations. The root must satisfy AppRootModel.

## Actions

## Getters
- `root: AppRootModel`
- `version: string`
- `gitCommit: string | undefined`
- `history: { canUndo: boolean; canRedo: boolean; undo(): void; redo(): void; } | undefined`
- `assemblyManager: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & {…} & {…} & {…} & {…} & IStateTreeNode<…>`

## Methods
- `menus() => Menu[]`

AssembliesMixin.text:
# AssembliesMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds `sessionAssemblies` (admin-aware, persisted-with-session assemblies) and `temporaryAssemblies` (used for ad-hoc read-vs-ref style assemblies).

## Actions
- `addSessionAssembly(conf: AnyConfiguration) => ConfigNodeProps<…> & ConfigNodeActions & ConfigNodeBrand<...>`
- `addAssembly(conf: AnyConfiguration) => void`
- `removeAssembly(name: string) => void`
- `removeSessionAssembly(assemblyName: string) => void`
- `addTemporaryAssembly(conf: AnyConfiguration) => ConfigNodeProps<…> & ConfigNodeActions & ConfigNodeBrand<...>`: used for read vs ref type assemblies.
- `removeTemporaryAssembly(name: string) => void`

## Getters
- `assemblies: (ConfigNodeProps<…> & ConfigNodeActions & ConfigNodeBrand<...>)[]`: sessionAssemblies plus jbrowse config assemblies. Does not include temporaryAssemblies; this is the list shown in the AssemblySelector dropdown.
- `assemblyNames: string[]`: names of the assemblies returned by the `assemblies` getter

## Properties
- `sessionAssemblies = types.stripDefault( types.array(assemblyConfigSchemasType), [], )`
- `temporaryAssemblies = types.stripDefault( types.array(assemblyConfigSchemasType), [], )`

## Methods
- `findAssemblyConf(name: unknown) => (ConfigNodeProps<…> & ConfigNodeActions & ConfigNodeBrand<ConfigurationSchemaType<…>>) | undefined`: The assembly config already carrying `name`, from any of the three arrays the assemblyManager draws on, or undefined.

Assembly.text:
# Assembly (Assembly Management model, core)

## Actions
- `setStatus(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Records what the in-flight load is doing. Its own actions block (rather than sitting next to setLoaded) so loadPre can hand `self.setStatus` to the adapters as a plain callback: it fires after awaits, outside the action that started the…
- `setRefNameMismatch(adapterCacheKey: string, mismatch: RefNameMismatch) => void`: Record that an adapter's reference names and this assembly's have nothing in common. Diagnostic only: `loadRefNameMap` still returns its map and the track still loads, because a wrong guess here must not take a working track away from…
- `setLoaded({…}: RefNameMaps & { regions: Region[]; cytobands: Feature[]; geneticCodes: Record<…>; }) => void`: Applies all load-time state in a single transaction so dependent autoruns fire once, with the precomputed lowercase/name lookups already in place by the time refNameAliases becomes observable.
- `setError(e: unknown) => void`
- `setLoadingP(p?: Promise<void> | undefined) => void`
- `loadPre() => Promise<void>`
- `load() => Promise<void>`: Resolves once regions + refNameAliases are set, and rejects with the load failure. Idempotent: concurrent callers share one attempt, and a failed attempt is discarded so the next call retries.

## Getters
- `name: string`
- `aliases: string[]`
- `displayName: string`
- `refNameColors: string[]`
- `allAliases: string[]`
- `initialized: boolean`
- `regions: BasicRegion[] | undefined`
- `allRefNames: string[] | undefined`: note: lowerCaseRefNameAliases not included here: this allows the list of refnames to be just the "normal casing", but things like getCanonicalRefName can resolve a lower-case name if needed
- `namesByCanonicalRefName: Map<string, string[]> | undefined`: canonical refName -> every name this assembly has for that sequence, canonical first. The inverse of `refNameAliases`, memoized here because the readers that want it want the whole table (the About dialog's alias listing) rather than one…
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`
- `refNames: string[] | undefined`
- `refNameToIndex: Map<string, number> | undefined`: memoized refName -> first region index, so getRefNameColor is O(1) instead of an O(n) indexOf per call (matters for assemblies with many contigs rendered in overview scalebars/rulers)

## Properties
- `configuration = types.safeReference(assemblyConfigType)`

## Methods
- `getConf(arg: string) => any`
- `hasName(name: string) => boolean`
- `getCanonicalRefName(refName: string) => string`: Returns the canonical refName for a given alias or refName. Note: The canonical name may differ from what's in the FASTA file when refNameAliases with override:true are configured. To get the name that matches the FASTA file, use…
- `getRefNameColor(refName: string) => string | undefined`
- `getRegionForRefName(refName: string) => BasicRegion | undefined`: The whole-contig region for a CANONICAL refName — its extents, and so the bounds anything placing a span on it has to clamp into. Undefined before `regions` loads, and for a refName this assembly doesn't have.
- `getGeneticCodeId(refName: string) => number`: NCBI genetic-code (translation table) id for a refName, from the assembly's `geneticCodes` config map (e.g. a mitochondrial contig = 2). Falls back to the standard code (1) for unlisted refNames.
- `getSeqAdapterRefName(canonicalRefName: string) => string`: Given a canonical refName, returns the refName used by the sequence adapter (what's in the FASTA file). Falls back to the input if no mapping exists.
- `getCanonicalRefName2(refName: string) => string`: The total canonical-refName resolver, for any name arriving from outside — off a feature, out of an RPC result, out of a session spec. A name the assembly does not know comes back unchanged, and so does one asked for before the aliases…
- `isValidRefName(refName: string) => boolean`
- `getRefNamePosition(refName: string) => number | undefined`: Where a refName — canonical or any alias — sits in this assembly's own order, which is what chromosome painting hands its palette out by. Canonicalized first because a name off a feature can be the FILE's spelling (`1` against a canonical…
- `getAliasesForRefName(refName: string) => string[]`: The other names this assembly has for the same sequence as `refName` — its aliases, whether the name handed in is an alias or the canonical name. `chr1`, `1` and `NC_000001.11` each answer with the other two.
- `getRefNameMapForAdapter(adapterConf: AdapterConf, options: BaseOptions) => Promise<RefNameAliases>`: get Map of `canonical-name -> adapter-specific-name`, memoized per adapter config so concurrent callers share one load
- `getRefNameMismatch(adapterCacheKey: string) => RefNameMismatch | undefined`: The empty-intersection verdict for an adapter under this assembly, if the map load reached one. Keyed by `adapterConfigCacheKey`, which is what a track already computes as its `rpcSessionId` — so a track looks up its own diagnostic with no…

AssemblyManager.text:
# AssemblyManager (Assembly Management model, core)

## Actions
- `removeAssembly(asm: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & { error: unknown; loadingP: Promise<…> | undefined; ... 10 more ...; refNameMismatches: Map<…>; } & ... 13 more ... & IStateT…`: private: you would generally want to add to manipulate jbrowse.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, or session.temporaryAssemblies instead of using this directly
- `addAssembly(configuration: any) => void`: private: you would generally want to add to manipulate jbrowse.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, or session.temporaryAssemblies instead of using this directly

## Getters
- `assemblyNameMap: Record<string, ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & { error: unknown; loadingP: Promise<…> | undefined; ... 10 more ...; refNameMismatches: Map<…>; } & ... 13 more ...…`
- `assemblyNamesList: string[]`: read via readConfObject, matching how the afterAttach autorun names the assemblies it creates: get() treats a name found here as "a config exists, its model is just not built yet", so the two must agree
- `configuredAssemblyNames: Set<string>`: Every name the *configs* answer to — each assembly's `name` and its `aliases`. What has knows before the models exist.
- `assemblyList: AnyConfigurationModel[]`: combined jbrowse.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, and session.temporaryAssemblies
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`

## Properties
- `assemblies = types.array(assemblyFactory(conf, pm))`: this is automatically managed by an autorun which looks in the parent session.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, and session.temporaryAssemblies

## Methods
- `getCanonicalAssemblyName(asmName: string) => string`
- `getDisplayName(asmName: string) => string`
- `get(asmName: string) => (ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & { error: unknown; ... 11 more ...; refNameMismatches: Map<...>; } & ... 13 more ... & IStateTreeNode<...>) |…`: The assembly `asmName` names, or undefined. Reports a name it doesn't know to `Core-handleUnrecognizedAssembly` so a plugin can go supply it, which is a side effect: a caller only asking *whether* the session has the assembly wants has…
- `has(asmName: string) => boolean`: Whether the session knows this assembly. Use this, not `get`, to ask only whether the assembly is present: `!has(name)` is exactly the condition under which `get` reports `name` to `Core-handleUnrecognizedAssembly`, so probing with `get`…
- `loadingAssembly(asmNames: string[]) => (ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & { error: unknown; ... 11 more ...; refNameMismatches: Map<...>; } & ... 13 more ... & IStateTreeNode<...>)…`: The first of `asmNames` that hasn't finished loading — the one a view blocked on them is waiting for, and whose `statusMessage` / `statusProgress` its spinner should show. Returns the assembly itself (a stable reference, so a consuming…
- `settleAssemblyResolution(assemblyName: string) => Promise<void>`: Wait out whatever might still be about to supply `assemblyName`, and resolve once nothing is.
- `waitForAssembly(assemblyName: string) => Promise<(ModelInstanceTypeProps<{ configuration: IMaybe<IReferenceType<IAnyType>>; }> & { ...; } & ... 13 more ... & IStateTreeNode<.…`: use this method instead of assemblyManager.get(assemblyName) to get an assembly with regions loaded
- `requireAssembly(assemblyName: string) => Promise<ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & { error: unknown; ... 11 more ...; refNameMismatches: Map<...>; } & ... 13 more ... & IStateTreeN…`: waitForAssembly, but a name that cannot be resolved is an error rather than an `undefined` for the caller to interpret.
- `getRefNameMapForAdapter(adapterConf: AdapterConf, assemblyName: string | undefined, opts: AssemblyBaseOpts) => Promise<RefNameAliases>`: The refName map for an adapter under `assemblyName`. Throws if the assembly cannot be resolved — see requireAssembly. No `assemblyName` at all is not a failure, just nothing to rename.
- `isValidRefName(refName: string, assemblyName: string) => boolean`

Base1DView.text:
# Base1DView (General model, core)

## Actions

- `setBpPerPx(val: number) => void`
- `setVolatileWidth(width: number) => void`

- `zoomIn() => void`

BaseChordDisplay.text:
# BaseChordDisplay (Display model, circular-view plugin)

What the circular view's chord and ribbon displays share: the features, the slice index a feature end is looked up in, and the lifecycle getters `ChordDisplayFrame` publishes. A track draws on the arcs of its own assemblies, so a one-genome variant track on a two-genome circle fetches and places only that genome's chords.

Composes BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `openErrorDialog() => void`
- `setFeatures(features: Feature[] | undefined) => void`
- `setHighlightedFeatureIds(ids: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `setVisibleFeatureIds(ids: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `reload() => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`: Overridable hook (default no-op): drop whatever `hoveredFeature` reports. The writing twin of that getter, and what `installClearHoverOnViewportChange` calls.
- `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record<string, unknown>, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…

## Getters
- `view: ModelInstanceTypeProps<_OverrideProps<Omit<Omit<…>, never>, { ...; }>> & ... 15 more ... & IStateTreeNode<...>`
- `trackAssemblyNames: string[]`: the track's assemblies that are on the circle, canonical and in the order the circle lays them out
- `fetchInert: boolean`: nothing of this track's is on the circle, so the fetch never runs; the SVG export's wait and the retry contract check both read it
- `loaded: boolean`
- `ready: boolean`
- `displayError: unknown`: what the error ring shows
- `svgReady: boolean`: the off-screen export gate, on the shared `computeSvgReady` policy. A radial display has no box to draw an error in, so the export fails rather than exporting a message
- `displayPhase: DisplayStatusPhase`
- `radiusPx: number`
- `bezierRadiusRatio: number`: how far from the center a chord across the circle passes, as a fraction of the radius; a shorter chord bows less, in proportion to its span
- `bezierRadius: number`
- `sliceIndex: Record<string, Slice>`: every slice of the circle, keyed by canonical assembly AND refName: two genomes on one circle can each carry a `chr1`. An elided slice answers to each refName it swallowed.
- `drawnFeatures: Feature[] | undefined`: what the chord components draw: `features`, narrowed to `visibleFeatureIds`
- `highlightedFeatureIdSet: Set<string> | undefined`
- `selectedFeatureId: string | undefined`
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: FC<…>`
- `DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{ id: IOptionalIType<ISimpleType<string>, [undefined]>; type: ISimpleType<string>; }> & { ...; } & { ...; } & IStateTreeNode…`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `hoveredFeature: unknown`: Overridable hook (default `undefined`): what the pointer is currently over, for readers **outside** the display. `LinearGenomeViewContainer` publishes it to `session.hovered`, the view-wide "what is the user pointing at" channel a plugin…
- `featureNoun: string`: Overridable hook (default `'feature'`): the SINGULAR word for one of the things this display draws, as a menu row or a chip says it — "Hide this read", "Showing 3 variants".
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: The widget `openFeatureWidget` opens for one of this display's features. Displays may override it. The default is the generic feature widget, for displays drawing plain features.

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.string`

## Methods
- `assemblyOf(assemblyName: string | undefined) => string | undefined`: the assembly on the circle a feature names, in whatever spelling the adapter wrote. A feature that names none, as a VCF record does not, is on the track's first assembly.
- `canonicalRefName(assemblyName: string, refName: string) => string`: a refName as the adapter wrote it, in the assembly's canonical spelling
- `sliceFor(assemblyName: string | undefined, refName: string) => Slice | undefined`: the slice one end of a feature lands on
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{ id: IOptionalIType<…>; type: ISimpleType<string>; }> & { ...; } & { ...; } & { ...; } & IStateTreeNode<...>; }`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`

BaseFeatureWidget.text:
# BaseFeatureWidget (Widget model, core)

The feature-details panel. `featureData` is the clicked feature with the track's and the session's `formatDetails` callbacks applied, derived on read from the raw feature the widget was opened with, so the same widget follows a config edit and survives its track being closed.

## Actions
- `setSequenceHoverPosition(pos: SequenceHoverPosition | undefined) => void`
- `setFeatureData(featureData: SimpleFeatureSerialized) => void`
- `clearFeatureData() => void`

## Getters
- `trackConfiguration: AnyConfigurationModel | undefined`: the config the track tier of `formatDetails` reads. The open track's own while it is open; after it is closed, the session's copy of the same config, which is why the widget records `trackId`
- `formatDetailsTiers: FormatDetailsTiers`
- `formatted: { feature?: SimpleFeatureSerialized | undefined; error?: Error | undefined; }`
- `maxDepth: number | undefined`: levels of subfeature card the panel renders; unset means no limit
- `featureData: SimpleFeatureSerialized | undefined`: the feature with every `formatDetails` callback applied
- `error: Error | undefined`

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.literal('BaseFeatureWidget')`
- `unformattedFeatureData = types.optional( types.frozen<MaybeSerializedFeat>(), undefined, )`: the feature as the click handed it over, before any callback ran. Persisted as `featureData`
- `view = types.safeReference( pluginManager.pluggableMstType('view', 'stateModel'), )`
- `track = types.safeReference( pluginManager.pluggableMstType('track', 'stateModel'), )`
- `trackId = types.maybe(types.string)`
- `trackType = types.maybe(types.string)`
- `sequenceFeatureDetails = types.optional(SequenceFeatureDetailsF(), {})`
- `descriptions = types.optional( types.frozen<Descriptors | undefined>(), undefined, )`
- `parentFeature = types.optional( types.frozen<ParentFeatureSummary | undefined>(), undefined, )`: names the feature this one was reached through, when it was reached through one -- a transcript clicked inside its gene

BaseInternetAccountModel.text:
# BaseInternetAccountModel (Internet Account model, core)

## Actions
- `getTokenFromUser(_resolve: (token: string) => void, _reject: (error: Error) => void) => void`: Must be implemented by a model extending or composing this one. Pass the user's token to `resolve`.
- `storeToken(token: string) => void`
- `retrieveToken() => string | undefined`
- `validateToken(token: string, _loc: UriLocation) => Promise<string>`: This can be used by an internetAccount to validate a token works before it is used. This is run when preAuthorizationInformation is requested, so it can be used to check that a token is valid before sending it to a worker thread. It…
- `removeToken() => void`: Clears the stored token. Also drops the in-memory cached promise so a subsequent `getToken` re-prompts / re-derives rather than handing back the token that was just invalidated.

# BreakpointSplitView (View model, breakpoint-split-view plugin)

Composes BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Hand-authored under `defaultSession.views`, with every setting written
directly on the view object. `views` is one entry per stacked panel, each
declaring the `assembly`, a `loc`, and the `tracks` to show. The two panels
flank a structural-variant breakpoint:
```js
{
  type: 'BreakpointSplitView',
  views: [
    { assembly: 'hg38', loc: 'chr1:1,000,000-1,100,000', tracks: ['alignments'] },
    { assembly: 'hg38', loc: 'chr5:2,000,000-2,100,000', tracks: ['alignments'] },
  ],
}
```
Each `tracks` entry can also be a `{ trackId, displaySnapshot }` object to
set per-panel display options (e.g. a shorter alignments height).

## Actions
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => void`
- `setHoveredOverlay(arg: OverlayHover | undefined) => void`: `undefined` when the pointer leaves a curve, and when the picture moves out from under it — see `overlayTransformKey`.
- `setInteractiveOverlay(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setShowIntraviewLinks(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setLinkViews(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setScrollZoom(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setShowHeader(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setMatchedTrackFeatures(obj: Record<string, Feature[][]>) => void`
- `reload() => void`: Re-run the overlay-feature fetch with no input change — what the Retry on its failure notification calls.
- `reverseViewOrder() => void`
- `squareView() => void`
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<BreakpointSplitViewCommands> | undefined) => void`
- `setViews(viewInits: BreakpointSplitViewInitView[]) => void`
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`

## Getters
- `ownViews: (ModelInstanceTypeProps<_OverrideProps<{ id: IOptionalIType<…>; displayName: IMaybe<…>; minimized: IOptionalIType<…>; }, { ...; }>> & ... 26 more ... & IStateT…`: The census entry for this view: its panels are views in their own right, and it holds no tracks outside them.
- `scrollZoom: boolean`: scroll-to-zoom is a global, personal preference resolved from the session; toggling it in any view applies everywhere
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<BreakpointSplitViewCommands & { unknown?: Record<…> | undefined; malformed?: Record<…> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolean | undefined; } & IStateTre…`: the launch state that still has something to apply — the gate the loading and import-form paths below read.
- `hasSomethingToShow: boolean`
- `initialized: boolean`: True on the import form too: with no panels and none pending there is nothing left to initialize, and `AppReadyMarker` reads a false here as the app still loading — which held `data-app-phase` at `loading` for as long as an empty split…
- `error: unknown`: Resolved, like LGV's and linear-comparative's: it folds in the sub-views, whose assemblies are what `initialized` waits on. Without them a failed assembly leaves `initialized` false forever with nothing to report, and an SVG export waiting…
- `showLoading: boolean`: Spinner instead of content, i.e. sub-views exist but haven't loaded their assemblies yet. Named to match LGV/dotplot/synteny/circular, since ViewContainer reads this name to publish `data-view-phase`.
- `loadingAssembly: (ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & { error: unknown; loadingP: Promise<…> | undefined; ... 10 more ...; refNameMismatches: Map<…>; } & ... 13 more ... & IStateTreeNo…`: The assembly whose load the spinner is waiting on. Delegated to the first sub-view that hasn't initialized, since each LGV already resolves this for itself; before the sub-views exist, `init` is what names them.
- `loading: ViewLoading | undefined`: What the loading screen says while `showLoading`, read off the assembly whose load is the wait; undefined otherwise.
- `showImportForm: boolean`: A failed assembly counts: the views it left behind never initialize, so there is nothing to show and no second attempt coming in this session. The form — which reports `error` in its banner — is then the only way forward, matching…
- `assemblies: ((ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & ... 13 more ... & IStateTreeNode<…>) | undefined)[]`: One assembly per row, index-aligned with `views`.
- `matchedTracks: OverlayTrack[]`: Find all track ids that match across multiple views, or return just the single view's track if only a single row is used
- `overlayTracks: OverlayTrack[]`: The matched tracks the overlay draws for — alignments and variants. The overlay fetch asks for these alone.
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Same name and same meaning as `FetchMixin.fetchInert`, on a view rather than a display: with no overlay track matched across the rows there is nothing for the overlay fetch to ask for, so `prepare` declines instead of running an empty…
- `overlayTransformKey: string`: Every number that moves the overlay under a stationary cursor, in one value — what `installClearHoverOnSurfaceMove` watches.
- `matchedTrackChunks: Map<string, MatchedChunks>`: Classifies each matched track and pairs its features, keyed by trackId. Everything here is a function of the fetched features alone, so it is deliberately kept out of `overlayMatches`, which additionally reads each track's layout: the…
- `overlayMatches: Map<string, OverlayMatch>`: Zero-arg cached getter: resolves each matched chunk's features to layout rectangles, returning a Map keyed by trackId. Mobx caches this across renders and only invalidates when the underlying feature or layout reads change — so scrolling…
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders its own displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.
- `ownTracks: AbstractTrackModel[]`: The tracks this view puts in the census — its own, not a nested view's.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('BreakpointSplitView')`
- `height = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultHeight)`: the height of the whole view in pixels, panels and overlay together
- `showIntraviewLinks = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: draw the links whose two ends land in the same panel, as well as the ones that cross between panels
- `linkViews = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: sync scroll and zoom across the panels, so panning one pans them all
- `interactiveOverlay = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: make the alignment squiggles drawn between the panels clickable, rather than a static overlay
- `showHeader = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: show the view's own header bar, above the panels' own
- `views = types.array( pluginManager.getViewType('LinearGenomeView').stateModel, )`
- `launch = types.frozen< LaunchInput<BreakpointSplitViewCommands> | undefined >()`: transient launch state: the declarative panels written on the view object as `views`, which need a measured width before they can be built rows. `preProcessSnapshot` moves them here off the snapshot, the afterAttach autorun applies them…
- `id = ElementId`
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar, keeping it in the session rather than closing it

## Methods
- `exportSvg(opts?: ExportSvgOptions) => Promise<string>`: renders the view to SVG markup, which it returns; saves it through FileSaver unless `save: false`
- `getMatchedTracks(trackConfigId: string) => OverlayTrack[]`: Get tracks with a given trackId across multiple views. Callers that index the result by view level (getTrackOverlayData, getMatchedFeaturesInLayout) rely on it staying aligned with `views` — which holds only because overlays are driven by…
- `getTrackOverlayData(trackId: string, yOffsetsOverride?: number[] | undefined) => {…}`: Per-render precompute for an overlay track. Resolves an OverlayLevel of geometry per view level, then returns getX/getY closures for converting feature layout records to SVG coordinates.
- `getMatchedFeaturesInLayout(trackConfigId: string, features: Feature[][]) => { feature: Feature; layout: LayoutRecord; level: number; clipLengthAtStartOfRead: number; }[][]`

- `rubberBandMenuItems() => { label: string; onClick: () => void; }[]`

# ChordSyntenyDisplay (Display model, circular-view plugin)

Config slots: docs topic "config:ChordSyntenyDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes BaseChordDisplay, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

The circular-view display for a `SyntenyTrack`: each alignment is drawn as a
ribbon between its span on one side and its mate's span on the other, so an
inversion reads as a twist. The track config below is what creates it; its
colors are the config slots on [](/docs/config/chordsyntenydisplay):
```js
{
  type: 'SyntenyTrack',
  trackId: 'volvox_self',
  name: 'Volvox self-alignment',
  assemblyNames: ['volvox', 'volvox'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PAFAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/volvox_self.paf',
    queryAssembly: 'volvox',
    targetAssembly: 'volvox',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'ChordSyntenyDisplay',
      displayId: 'volvox_self-ChordSyntenyDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```
A track aligning two assemblies needs both of them on the circle, which is
the view's `assembly: ['hg38', 'mm39']` — see the
[synteny track guide](/docs/config_guides/synteny_track).

## Actions
- `setColorBy(colorBy: "chromosome" | "default" | "strand") => void`
- `onRibbonClick(feature: Feature) => void`
- `reload() => void`: refetch, and run a reorder this launch still owes, which is how the error ring's Retry reaches a reorder that failed
- `openErrorDialog() => void`
- `setFeatures(features: Feature[] | undefined) => void`
- `setHighlightedFeatureIds(ids: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `setVisibleFeatureIds(ids: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`: Overridable hook (default no-op): drop whatever `hoveredFeature` reports. The writing twin of that getter, and what `installClearHoverOnViewportChange` calls.
- `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record<string, unknown>, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…

## Getters
- `colorBy: "chromosome" | "default" | "strand"`: what a ribbon's hue says: the `color` config slot, the chromosome of the circle's first genome it joins (that arc's ideogram color), or the strand. The strand is also the twist in every mode
- `ready: boolean`: `loaded`, and no reorder this launch asked for still owed. Ribbons drawn before it would be drawn against the arcs it is about to move; a reorder that failed keeps this false and shows as `displayPhase` error, so a capture never commits…
- `displayError: unknown`: the fetch's error, or else the owed reorder's
- `featureNoun: string`
- `legendColor: string | undefined`: the ribbon fill the circle's key shows, when every ribbon shares one
- `ribbonFill: (feature: Feature) => string`: the resting fill of each ribbon under `colorBy`
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: the panel the linear synteny displays open for the same record, so a ribbon clicked on the circle and a ribbon clicked in a synteny view share one drawer entry
- `view: ModelInstanceTypeProps<_OverrideProps<Omit<Omit<…>, never>, { ...; }>> & ... 15 more ... & IStateTreeNode<...>`
- `trackAssemblyNames: string[]`: the track's assemblies that are on the circle, canonical and in the order the circle lays them out
- `fetchInert: boolean`: nothing of this track's is on the circle, so the fetch never runs; the SVG export's wait and the retry contract check both read it
- `loaded: boolean`
- `svgReady: boolean`: the off-screen export gate, on the shared `computeSvgReady` policy. A radial display has no box to draw an error in, so the export fails rather than exporting a message
- `displayPhase: DisplayStatusPhase`
- `radiusPx: number`
- `bezierRadiusRatio: number`: how far from the center a chord across the circle passes, as a fraction of the radius; a shorter chord bows less, in proportion to its span
- `bezierRadius: number`
- `sliceIndex: Record<string, Slice>`: every slice of the circle, keyed by canonical assembly AND refName: two genomes on one circle can each carry a `chr1`. An elided slice answers to each refName it swallowed.
- `drawnFeatures: Feature[] | undefined`: what the chord components draw: `features`, narrowed to `visibleFeatureIds`
- `highlightedFeatureIdSet: Set<string> | undefined`
- `selectedFeatureId: string | undefined`
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: FC<…>`
- `DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{ id: IOptionalIType<ISimpleType<string>, [undefined]>; type: ISimpleType<string>; }> & { ...; } & { ...; } & IStateTreeNode…`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `hoveredFeature: unknown`: Overridable hook (default `undefined`): what the pointer is currently over, for readers **outside** the display. `LinearGenomeViewContainer` publishes it to `session.hovered`, the view-wide "what is the user pointing at" channel a plugin…

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('ChordSyntenyDisplay')`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `id = ElementId`

## Methods
- `alignmentsBetween(referenceAssembly: string, currentAssembly: string) => AlignmentData[]`: the held alignments joining two assemblies on the circle, in canonical refNames and oriented reference side first, which is what the view's reorder reads instead of fetching the file again
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `renderSvg(_opts: ViewExportSvgOptions & { theme?: ThemeOptions | undefined; }) => Promise<Element | null>`
- `assemblyOf(assemblyName: string | undefined) => string | undefined`: the assembly on the circle a feature names, in whatever spelling the adapter wrote. A feature that names none, as a VCF record does not, is on the track's first assembly.
- `canonicalRefName(assemblyName: string, refName: string) => string`: a refName as the adapter wrote it, in the assembly's canonical spelling
- `sliceFor(assemblyName: string | undefined, refName: string) => Slice | undefined`: the slice one end of a feature lands on
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{ id: IOptionalIType<…>; type: ISimpleType<string>; }> & { ...; } & { ...; } & { ...; } & IStateTreeNode<...>; }`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks

# ChordVariantDisplay (Display model, circular-view plugin)

Config slots: docs topic "config:ChordVariantDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes BaseChordDisplay, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

The circular-view display for a `VariantTrack` of structural variants;
translocations are drawn as chords across the circle. The track config below
is what creates it; its colors are the config slots on
[](/docs/config/chordvariantdisplay):
```js
{
  type: 'VariantTrack',
  trackId: 'sv',
  name: 'Structural variants',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'VcfTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/sv.vcf.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'ChordVariantDisplay',
      displayId: 'sv-ChordVariantDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```

CircularView.text:
# CircularView (View model, circular-view plugin)

Composes BaseViewModel, DiagonalizeProgressMixin, ImportFormSyntenyMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Hand-authored under `defaultSession.views`, with every setting written
directly on the view object. `assembly` picks the genome, a `tracks` entry may
carry display config inline, and `displayedRegionNames` keeps an assembly's
alt/unplaced contigs off the circle:
```js
{
  type: 'CircularView',
  assembly: 'hg38',
  displayedRegionNames: ['chr1', 'chr2', 'chr3'],
  tracks: [{ trackId: 'my-sv-vcf', strokeColor: 'red' }],
}
```
`assembly` also takes a list, for a synteny ribbon plot: each
assembly lays its contigs out in turn, so the first genome takes one arc of
the circle and the second the next, and a `SyntenyTrack` covering both draws
a ribbon per alignment between them. `displayedRegionNames` keyed by assembly
restricts each genome separately, and `autoDiagonalize` reorders the second
to follow the first:
```js
{
  type: 'CircularView',
  assembly: ['hg38', 'mm39'],
  displayedRegionNames: { hg38: ['chr1', 'chr2'] },
  tracks: ['hg38_vs_mm39'],
  autoDiagonalize: true,
}
```

## Actions
- `fitToWindow() => void`: size the figure so it exactly fills the smaller of the view's two dimensions
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => number`
- `setHeight(newHeight: number) => number`
- `setShowLegend(flag: boolean) => void`
- `rotateClockwiseButton() => void`
- `rotateCounterClockwiseButton() => void`
- `rotate(delta: number) => void`
- `resetView() => void`: reset rotation, pan, and zoom back to the default fit-to-window view
- `zoomInButton() => void`
- `zoomOutButton() => void`
- `setBpPerPx(newVal: number) => void`
- `zoomToPoint(newBpPerPx: number, cursorX: number, cursorY: number) => void`: zoom toward/away from a point on the figure, keeping whatever is under it visually fixed. The point is its offset in screen px from the middle of the circle — what `offsetFromCenter` in the component hands back
- `setDisplayedRegions(regions: Region[]) => void`
- `activateTrackSelector() => Widget | undefined`
- `toggleTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `setError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<CircularViewCommands> | undefined) => void`
- `clearView() => void`: back to the import form: no regions, no tracks, no pending launch and no error from the one before
- `showTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: any, displayInitialSnapshot?: any, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => any`
- `addTrackConf(configuration: Record<string, unknown>, initialSnapshot?: any) => any`
- `hideTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `openExportDialog() => void`
- `openReorderChromosomesDialog() => void`
- `autoDiagonalize() => Promise<void>`: The init-time reorder, behind the "Reordering chromosomes" screen `withDiagonalizeProgress` drives.
- `exportSvg(opts?: ViewExportSvgOptions) => Promise<string>`: renders the view to SVG markup, which it returns; saves it through FileSaver unless `save: false`
- `launchTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: any, displayInitialSnapshot?: any) => Promise<any>`: showTrack for a track whose display state model may be lazily loaded: loads it, then shows
- `launchToggleTrack(trackId: string) => Promise<boolean>`: toggleTrack with launchTrack's loading behavior
- `launchTrackConf(configuration: Record<string, unknown>, initialSnapshot?: any) => Promise<any>`: `addTrackConf` with `launchTrack`'s loading behavior, for a track handed over inline rather than from a session list
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`
- `resizeWidth(distance: number) => number`
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setAwaitingAutoDiagonalize(arg: boolean) => void`
- `beginAutoDiagonalize(requested: boolean) => void`: Declare the gate at the top of one init apply pass: a reorder is pending iff THIS init asked for one. Assigning rather than raising is what hands the gate over cleanly — a superseded init that asked for a reorder and then skipped it would…
- `finishAutoDiagonalize() => void`: A reorder resolved, the init's or a manual one, so the view on screen is the diagonalized one — open the gate.
- `setDiagonalizeError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setDiagonalizeCancel(arg?: (() => void) | undefined) => void`
- `cancelAutoDiagonalize() => void`: Abort an in-flight auto-diagonalize; `withDiagonalizeProgress`'s finally clears the wait flag, revealing the (undiagonalized) view.
- `setImportFormSyntenyTrack(idx: number, val: ImportFormSyntenyTrack) => void`
- `clearImportFormSyntenyTracks() => void`: Drop the pending selections once a launch has applied them. Left in place they outlive the form: "Return to import form" would reopen on a finished upload from the previous launch, and a pair whose assemblies no longer match it reads as an…

## Getters
- `ownTracks: any[]`: The census entry for this view: the tracks it holds itself. Declared rather than derived — see `BaseViewModel.ownTracks`.
- `width: number`
- `effectivePaddingPx: number`: `paddingPx`, capped so it cannot eat a small box.
- `effectiveSpacingPx: number`: `spacingPx`, capped so the inter-chromosome gaps cannot take the ring.
- `fitRadiusPx: number`: the radius the current box has room for — what `fitToWindow` aims at, and the scale `effectiveSpacingPx` measures itself against. A pure function of the box, so neither reads back a value derived from it
- `circumferencePx: number`
- `radiusPx: number`
- `bpPerRadian: number`
- `centerXY: [number, number]`
- `totalBp: number`
- `maxBpPerPx: number`
- `minBpPerPx: number`
- `atMaxBpPerPx: boolean`
- `atMinBpPerPx: boolean`
- `figureSize: number`: figure is always square, so width === height
- `figureOriginXY: [number, number]`: top-left of the figure within the view's box, then shifted by the zoom-to-cursor pan.
- `elidedRegions: SliceRegion[]`: this is displayedRegions, post-processed to elide regions that are too small to see reasonably. A run of them never crosses from one assembly into the next, so each genome's arcs stay its own.
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<CircularViewCommands & { unknown?: Record<…> | undefined; malformed?: Record<…> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolean | undefined; } & IStateTreeNode<.…`: the launch state that still has something to apply — the gate the loading and import-form paths below read.
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `chordSyntenyDisplays: ChordSyntenyDisplaySelf[]`: Every ribbon display under this view's tracks; a chromosome reorder reads its alignments from these. Filtered by `type` rather than taken as `tracks[i].displays[0]`, for the reason the dotplot's `dotplotDisplays` gives.
- `canDiagonalize: boolean`: Whether a chromosome reorder has anything to do: a ribbon track to take alignments from, and exactly the two genomes a mirrored layout is defined for. One is a self-alignment, with no second arc to reorder; three or more have no layout in…
- `launchAssemblyNames: string[]`: The assemblies a pending launch names, which the gates below wait on before `displayedRegions` exist. A blob carrying only tracks names none, and waiting on one nobody named never ends.
- `initialized: boolean`
- `assemblyErrors: string | undefined`
- `error: unknown`
- `hasSomethingToShow: boolean`
- `showLoading: boolean`: Whether to show a loading indicator instead of the import form or view
- `loadingAssembly: (ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & { error: unknown; loadingP: Promise<…> | undefined; ... 10 more ...; refNameMismatches: Map<…>; } & ... 13 more ... & IStateTreeNo…`: The assembly whose load the spinner is waiting on. A pending launch names them before displayedRegions exist, so it is the source until then — the same order `initialized` above resolves in.
- `loading: ViewLoading | undefined`: What the loading screen says while `showLoading`, read off the assembly whose load is the wait; undefined otherwise.
- `showView: boolean`: Whether the view is fully initialized and ready to display
- `showImportForm: boolean`: `!hasSomethingToShow || !!error`, the same predicate as every other view, with `disableImportForm` suppressing the whole thing rather than only its first half.
- `status: ViewStatus`: The view's lifecycle as one value — ready, error, loading or noRegions — for a host that draws its own chrome and has to render all four. Same shape and same precedence as the linear view's, through `computeViewStatus`.
- `regionHost: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & { ...; } & { ...; } & { ...; } & IStateTreeNode<…>`: The node a linear display's foundation reads as its view: the circumference unrolled into a strip. A display registered for the linear genome view draws on this view as a ring of that strip, so `containingHost` answers this rather than the…
- `chordRadiusPx: number`: Where the chord displays start: inside the innermost ring, or at the ruler when the view holds none.
- `staticSlices: Slice[]`
- `legendSpec: LegendSpec`: one row per track: its name beside the color or ramp it paints with
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders its own displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.
- `ownViews: AbstractViewModel[]`: The views nested directly inside this one, which the census counts as views in their own right — a synteny stack's genome rows, a breakpoint split view's panels.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('CircularView') as unknown as string`: this is a string instead of the const literal 'CircularView' to reduce some typescripting strictness, but you should pass the string 'CircularView' to the model explicitly
- `offsetRadians = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultOffsetRadians)`: similar to offsetPx in linear genome view
- `bpPerPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultBpPerPx)`: the zoom level, base-pairs per pixel. Capped by `minimumRadiusPx`, and refit over by the first resize unless `autoFit` is false.
- `autoFit = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: whether the view keeps re-fitting to its container on resize. Cleared once the user manually zooms/pans so their view (persisted via bpPerPx/offsetRadians) is preserved across resizes and reloads.
- `tracks = types.array( pluginManager.pluggableMstType('track', 'stateModel'), )`
- `hideVerticalResizeHandle = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: chrome switch, for an embed that drives the view itself
- `hideTrackSelectorButton = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: chrome switch, for an embed that drives the view itself
- `disableImportForm = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: suppress the import form even on an error — what the SV inspector's circle wants, since its assembly comes from the sheet beside it and a form there would offer a control that cannot work
- `showLegend = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: a key naming each track's ring, chords or ribbons in the corner
- `height = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultHeight)`: the height of the view in pixels. The circle auto-fits its container, so this is what sizes the drawing.
- `displayedRegions = types.stripDefault(types.frozen<Region[]>(), [])`: the regions the circle lays out, one arc each, in this order. `displayedRegionNames` names the same thing by refName and is the shorter form.
- `minimumRadiusPx = types.stripDefault( types.number, defaultMinimumRadiusPx, )`: how far in the circle may be zoomed, as a floor on the radius; it is what caps bpPerPx
- `spacingPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultSpacingPx)`: the gap drawn between adjacent chromosome arcs
- `paddingPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultPaddingPx)`: blank margin between the circle and the edge of the figure
- `minVisibleWidth = types.stripDefault( types.number, defaultMinVisibleWidth, )`: arcs thinner than this many pixels are elided instead of drawn, so a few thousand unplaced contigs do not become a ring of hairlines
- `trackSelectorType = types.stripDefault(types.string, 'hierarchical')`: vestigial: the hierarchical selector is the only one that exists, so this value is ignored. Retained because saved sessions and share links persist it.
- `launch = types.frozen<LaunchInput<CircularViewCommands> | undefined>()`: transient launch state: the settings written on the view object that need resolving before they can be view state — the assembly the circle is drawn from, the refNames to restrict it to, chord track recipes. `preProcessSnapshot` moves them…
- `id = ElementId`
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar, keeping it in the session rather than closing it

## Methods
- `menuItems() => MenuItem[]`: return the view menu items
- `tracksMenuItem() => MenuItem`: each track's own menu, which on a linear view hangs off its label and on the circle has nowhere else to go

# CoarseTierMixin (Mixin model, core) The zoomed-out tier a display draws in place of its detail: the density band's bins, MAF's summary bars. The verdict stays exactly what `RegionTooLargeMixin` derives, and this mixin adds the swap decision, the per-region payloads and the read that fills them, through the shared fetch skeleton on its own rotation so the detail fetch's cancel never reaches it. ## Actions - `setCoarseTier(entries: CoarseTierEntry

[], read: CoarseTierRead) => void` - `clearCoarseTier() => void` - `setCoarseTierLoading(loading: boolean) => void` - `fetchCoarseTier(_read: CoarseTierRead, _ctx: FetchContext) => Promise>`: Overridable hook (no-op base): the coarse read over `read.regions`, answering one payload per region it covered or a refusal. `ctx` is the skeleton's — its `callRpc` carries the signal and the status slot, and `isStale` guards any write… ## Getters - `coarseAdapterSlot: string | undefined`: Overridable hook (default none): the slot on the track's adapter the coarse source sits in — `densityAdapter`, `summaryAdapter`. With no slot there is no source and the tier never stands in. - `coarseTierMode: CoarseTierMode`: Overridable hook (default `auto`): the user's override, where the display offers one. - `coarseTierPastThreshold: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the display's own line past which `auto` swaps before the gate refuses anything — a bp/px slot, a span floor. - `coarseTierGated: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the coarse read is a feature download the byte gate has to measure. The gate then measures the coarse adapter while the tier is up, its refusal is the banner, the detail fetch stands down outright since… - `coarseReadKey: unknown`: Overridable hook (default `''`): what the read depends on beyond its span and its adapter — a zoom bucket, the settings axis. A value compared structurally, so a held read whose key differs re-reads. - `coarseSourceConfig: unknown`: The coarse source's config, read off the live track config so a re-pointed adapter follows. - `hasCoarseSource: boolean` - `coarseTierActive: boolean`: Whether the coarse tier stands in for the detail right now. - `coarseTierStandsIn: boolean`: Overridable hook (default: the tier's verdict) — whether the tier is standing in for the detail on screen right now. A display whose tier needs somewhere to draw narrows it: canvas adds the view geometry the draw is mapped through,… - `gateMeasuresCoarse: boolean`: The byte gate is measuring the coarse read rather than the detail fetch, so its verdict is about the tier on screen. - `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: `RegionTooLargeMixin`'s hook: measure the adapter of the fetch that is about to run, so the estimate and the budget describe one file. - `gateRefusesDetail: boolean`: The gate's refusal is about the detail fetch, so that fetch owes the re-measure the gate releases through. - `coarseTierIssueKey: { adapter: (Record & { type: string; }) | undefined; read: unknown; }`: The whole key a read is held under: the coarse adapter and the display's own term. - `fetchSuspended: boolean`: `MultiRegionDisplayMixin`'s hook, from `resolveFetchSuspended` over `coarseTierStandsIn`. - `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The foundation's phase with the too-large banner swapped for the tier — see `coarseTierDisplayPhase`. - `svgReady: boolean`: The export gate under the same swap — see `coarseTierSvgReady`. - `drawsWhenTooLarge: boolean`: `renderDisplaySvg`'s hook: the export paints the tier in place of the too-large note, the same swap the chrome makes on screen — unless the note is about the coarse read itself.

ComparativeFetchMixin.text:
# ComparativeFetchMixin (Mixin model, core)

The fetch foundation of the two comparative displays (LinearSyntenyDisplay, DotplotDisplay): `KeyedFetchMixin` — `FetchMixin`'s rotation, loading flag, error, status, durable cancel and retry, plus the `currentFetchKey` / `loadedFetchKey` freshness pair the LGV global family runs on — and, on top, the two-way loading answer a shared canvas wants — `loading` off the `fetchLanded` hook, `refetching` off `isLoading` — and the one-shot reversed-assembly flag.

Composes KeyedFetchMixin, FetchMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setAssembliesSwapped(arg: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchResult(commit: () => void, key: FetchKey) => void`: The commit half of a keyed fetch: run the display's own store in the same transaction as the key stamp, so no observer can see fresh data under a stale key or the reverse. As the only writer of `loadedFetchKey`, this action makes…
- `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter — the shared skeleton's reload epoch makes that bump override the freshness gate, even against a fetch that commits mid-reload, so nothing here has to remember to invalidate for the retry's sake)…
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and lands in a durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does NOT bump fetchGeneration — so the fetch autoruns don't immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, an action of its own because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.

## Getters
- `fetchLanded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): a fetch has completed and data is present, even if it mapped zero features. Not a feature-count test — an empty-but-finished fetch has landed, or an empty plot spins its overlay forever. Each display…
- `hasDrawable: boolean`: Overridable hook: the display holds something an SVG export can draw. Defaults to `fetchLanded`; the dotplot answers with its instance geometry rather than its `geometry` computed, because `svgReady` is polled outside any reactive context…
- `loading: boolean`: First load, nothing on screen yet: drives the full striped overlay. Deliberately not `&& isLoading`, which would blink the overlay off during the pre-fetch debounce gap. Excludes `error` so error UI and loading UI never show at once, and…
- `refetching: boolean`: A fetch is running over a stale plot still on screen (zoom, reorder, pan past the buffer): drives a corner indicator rather than the full overlay, so a viewport change does not mask what is drawn.
- `svgReady: boolean`: Off-screen SVG export gate, the shared `computeSvgReady` policy every display runs. Neither comparative display has a `regionTooLarge` state (LOD gates the fetch, not region size). `fetchInert` is the extra terminal, so an export cannot…
- `viewSignature: string | undefined`: Overridable hook, the one freshness input a display supplies: the signature of what the current *view* calls for — its block set (`blockKeySignature`) plus any view-derived fetch tier, like HiC's binsize; both comparative views' region…
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the held data answers the key, but this display knows it is not what the screen will settle on — a dependent fetch of its own is still out, or a fetch input it writes itself has moved. The same hook…
- `currentFetchKey: FetchKey | undefined`: Key of the fetch the current view, settings and adapter call for. The fetch skeleton's freshness key: captured at issue, compared against the stamp above, and written to it at commit. Its identity survives a recomputation onto equal…
- `dataCurrent: boolean`: The shared freshness answer every foundation gives: data has been committed (`loadedFetchKey` is only ever written beside it), it was fetched for the current view and settings, and the display is not about to supersede it itself. A pan…
- `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active
- `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished…
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately never fetches, so it holds no data and none is coming. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off.
- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the…
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by `computeActivityPhase`: a load this display depends on beyond its primary fetch has not landed for the first time, so the frame the primary fetch calls current is still missing something. Multi-way…

# DiagonalizeProgressMixin (Mixin model, core)

The auto-diagonalize lifecycle state shared by the comparative views (LinearSyntenyView, DotplotView, CircularView): the in-flight wait, its live RPC status and signal, and the flag that gates `settled` so a screenshot or browser test can't capture a pre-reorder hairball.

## Actions
- `setAwaitingAutoDiagonalize(arg: boolean) => void`
- `beginAutoDiagonalize(requested: boolean) => void`: Declare the gate at the top of one init apply pass: a reorder is pending iff THIS init asked for one. Assigning rather than raising is what hands the gate over cleanly — a superseded init that asked for a reorder and then skipped it would…
- `finishAutoDiagonalize() => void`: A reorder resolved, the init's or a manual one, so the view on screen is the diagonalized one — open the gate.
- `setDiagonalizeError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setDiagonalizeCancel(arg?: (() => void) | undefined) => void`
- `cancelAutoDiagonalize() => void`: Abort an in-flight auto-diagonalize; `withDiagonalizeProgress`'s finally clears the wait flag, revealing the (undiagonalized) view.

# DotplotDisplay (Display model, dotplot-view plugin)

Config slots: docs topic "config:DotplotDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes BaseDisplay, ComparativeFetchMixin, KeyedFetchMixin, FetchMixin, LodTierInfoMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setRpcData(data: DotplotRpcData, warnings: ComparativeWarning[]) => void`: Commits a fetch result and the warnings it raised, tagged with the key it was fetched for. One action, not three: the warnings describe this result, so writing them separately let a failed refetch leave the last result's warnings standing…
- `setInstanceData(data: DotplotInstanceData | undefined) => void`
- `setHoveredSegmentIdx(idx: number) => void`: Written by the view's `setHoveredFeature`, which points the whole plot's hover at one hit — never per display from a component, so the N writes land in one MobX batch.
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`: Overridable hook (default no-op): drop whatever `hoveredFeature` reports. The writing twin of that getter, and what `installClearHoverOnViewportChange` calls.
- `reload() => void`: base display reload does nothing, see specialized displays for details
- `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record<string, unknown>, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…
- `setAssembliesSwapped(arg: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchResult(commit: () => void, key: FetchKey) => void`: The commit half of a keyed fetch: run the display's own store in the same transaction as the key stamp, so no observer can see fresh data under a stale key or the reverse. As the only writer of `loadedFetchKey`, this action makes…
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and lands in a durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does NOT bump fetchGeneration — so the fetch autoruns don't immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, an action of its own because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.
- `setAdapterHeader(read: AdapterRead<unknown>) => void`

## Getters
- `view: DotplotViewModel`: The plot this display draws into. One getter rather than a `getContainingView` cast per reader, the same way `LinearSyntenyDisplay.view` answers it.
- `displayKey: number`: Stable slot on the view-shared backend. Hashed from the node id, not taken from the track's index, so hiding or reordering a sibling can't hand this display another's buffer.
- `fetchLanded: boolean`: `ComparativeFetchMixin`'s hook: a fetch has completed (data is present, even if it mapped zero features). Not a feature-count test — an empty-but-finished fetch has landed, otherwise an empty plot spins the loading overlay forever.
- `hasDrawable: boolean`: `ComparativeFetchMixin`'s hook, answered with the instance geometry rather than `fetchLanded` or the `geometry` computed: `svgReady` is polled outside any reactive context, and a `geometry` read there recolors every segment per poll.
- `computedColors: Uint32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | undefined`: Main-thread-computed per-segment colors — the gpuProps half of the rpcProps/gpuProps split. A colorBy change recomputes this alone, without re-walking a single CIGAR.
- `paintedRefNamePosition: RefNamePosition | undefined`: Where a refName sits in whichever axis' assembly `colorBy` names — `Assembly.getRefNamePosition`, alias-aware — which the chromosome-painting modes hand the palette out by. Undefined for every other mode, and while the assembly is still…
- `paintedField: string`: The view's `colorByField` as this plot paints it. 'reference' is the horizontal axis, the one diagonalize orders the vertical against, so it paints as 'query' — the dotplot twin of `LinearSyntenyDisplay.paintedField`, which resolves it per…
- `trackColor: string`: This track's slot in the plot's palette, used by the `track` field. Assigned by the view, not locally: pinning a color on one track shifts which automatic slots its siblings can take.
- `trackId: string`
- `geometry: { colors: Uint32Array<ArrayBufferLike>; x1: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; y1: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; ... 6 more ...; baseV: number; } | undefined`: Instance positions joined with the computed colors: what the backends upload and what SVG export draws. The view's upload autorun reads this, so a palette change re-uploads without rebuilding geometry.
- `hoveredFeatureIdx: number`: Index into `rpcData`'s per-FEATURE arrays of the alignment the pointer is over, or -1. Derived rather than stored, so it cannot disagree with `hoveredSegmentIdx` about which alignment that is.
- `tooltipLines: string[] | undefined`: The hovered feature's tooltip, as lines, or undefined when nothing is hovered. The dotplot twin of `LinearSyntenyDisplay.tooltipLines`; both feed `ComparativeTooltip`, which renders lines as text nodes — see `getDotplotTooltipLines`.
- `hoveredFeatureHighlight: DotplotHoverHighlight | undefined`: The hovered feature redrawn over the canvas: an SVG path of its segments in plot px, plus its own packed color as CSS.
- `fetchRegions: Region[]`: The h-axis fetch window: the visible content blocks expanded by the shared pan buffer and snapped outward to a buffer-sized grid, so a pan within the buffer neither refetches nor exposes an unfetched strip, and zoomed out it collapses to…
- `viewSignature: string`: `KeyedFetchMixin`'s hook, this display's half of `currentFetchKey`: the fetch-input signature (see fetchKey.ts) for the view's current state. The mixin appends the settings and adapter axes. Reactive: recomputes when either axis's zoom or…

- `displayPhase: DisplayStatusPhase`: The display's own mutually-exclusive state, the way every LGV display publishes one — so `AppReadyMarker` counts this display's fetch, and the app stops reporting itself ready over a plot that is still working. Ranked by…
- `warnings: ComparativeWarning[]`: Per-render fetch warnings, plus the load-time reversed-assembly hint.
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: FC<…>`
- `DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{ id: IOptionalIType<ISimpleType<string>, [undefined]>; type: ISimpleType<string>; }> & { ...; } & { ...; } & IStateTreeNode…`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `hoveredFeature: unknown`: Overridable hook (default `undefined`): what the pointer is currently over, for readers **outside** the display. `LinearGenomeViewContainer` publishes it to `session.hovered`, the view-wide "what is the user pointing at" channel a plugin…

- `loading: boolean`: First load, nothing on screen yet: drives the full striped overlay. Deliberately not `&& isLoading`, which would blink the overlay off during the pre-fetch debounce gap. Excludes `error` so error UI and loading UI never show at once, and…
- `refetching: boolean`: A fetch is running over a stale plot still on screen (zoom, reorder, pan past the buffer): drives a corner indicator rather than the full overlay, so a viewport change does not mask what is drawn.
- `svgReady: boolean`: Off-screen SVG export gate, the shared `computeSvgReady` policy every display runs. Neither comparative display has a `regionTooLarge` state (LOD gates the fetch, not region size). `fetchInert` is the extra terminal, so an export cannot…
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the held data answers the key, but this display knows it is not what the screen will settle on — a dependent fetch of its own is still out, or a fetch input it writes itself has moved. The same hook…
- `currentFetchKey: FetchKey | undefined`: Key of the fetch the current view, settings and adapter call for. The fetch skeleton's freshness key: captured at issue, compared against the stamp above, and written to it at commit. Its identity survives a recomputation onto equal…

- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the…
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by `computeActivityPhase`: a load this display depends on beyond its primary fetch has not landed for the first time, so the frame the primary fetch calls current is still missing something. Multi-way…
- `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,…
- `adapterHeader: unknown`: The header of the adapter config the display holds, undefined until its read lands.
